headline: Ahead of the October Special Town Meeting, Southborough boards finalized positions on housing, stormwater, water line funding, and contested CPA-funded recreation projects.
synopsis: Ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting, town boards finalized reports and recommendations on warrant articles addressing infrastructure, zoning, and finances. The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance a $217,318 CPA request for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge, while the Advisory Committee issued unfavorable recommendations for both the bridge and a $1 million golf course irrigation overhaul. The Advisory Committee supported spending $240,000 from water retained earnings for water connections near the Parkerville Road landfill and clarified that a proposed stormwater enterprise fund would not levy fees without future Town Meeting approval. The Zoning Board of Appeals backed a two-family zoning amendment as drafted, though the Advisory Committee recommended against it due to lot size and septic capacity concerns. Meanwhile, the Select Board reviewed initial findings from a town governance study examining Southborough's administrative structure and town manager authority.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail bridge CPA funding advances to Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send the $217,318 CPA funding request to Special Town Meeting as written, despite formal opposition from both the Advisory Committee and Select Board.
top_items.body: The Trails Committee and Community Preservation Committee debated whether to scale back the project or introduce a floor amendment before deciding to present Article 4 as originally drafted. The article requests $217,318 in additional Community Preservation Act funds on top of an existing $211,000 allocation, setting the total cost for the 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian bridge along Route 30 at $428,550. While trail advocates highlighted pedestrian safety and regional connectivity, the Advisory Committee unanimously opposed the measure and the Select Board voted 1-4 against recommendation, citing high construction costs.

top_items.title: Debate over golf course irrigation funding ahead of vote
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee recommended against spending CPA funds on an approximately $1 million irrigation system at the Southborough Golf Club, while the Golf Committee coordinated outreach to support Article 3.
top_items.body: The Golf Committee finalized informational flyers and agreed to advance its funding plan to the October 17 Special Town Meeting without floor amendments. The proposal relies on roughly $433,546 in additional CPA funds, extending a $553,750 CPA appropriation from 2024, along with $100,000 to $150,000 from the golf revolving fund. The Advisory Committee opposed the measure, arguing that municipal golf course capital expenses should not be shifted to town taxpayers when the facility was intended to be self-sustaining.

top_items.title: Boards split on two-family dwelling zoning amendment
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to support Article 2 as drafted, while the Advisory Committee voted to recommend against adoption at Special Town Meeting.
top_items.body: The proposed zoning amendment would alter town code regarding two-family dwellings, removing certain minimum lot references across subsections. While the Zoning Board of Appeals decided against last-minute edits and voted to support the warrant article as written, the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation. The Advisory Committee cited concerns about removing the two-year ownership requirement, lot sizes in Residential B zones, reliance on percolation tests for septic capacity, and the limited practical safeguards provided by special permits.

top_items.title: Water connection funds recommended for Parkerville landfill area
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Town Meeting approval of Article 7, allocating $240,000 from water retained earnings for two homes near the landfill.
top_items.body: Article 7 seeks $240,000 from water enterprise retained earnings to extend a water main and connect two residences near the Parkerville Road landfill following contamination testing. The Advisory Committee confirmed with the Select Board chair that town funds will cover the service connections from the street directly into the homes before unanimously approving their recommendation report.

top_items.title: Advisory clarifies stormwater enterprise fund creates no fees
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee finalized report wording for Article 5, emphasizing that establishing the enterprise fund structure does not implement any fees.
top_items.body: Ahead of Special Town Meeting, the Advisory Committee clarified that Article 5 is solely an accounting mechanism that establishes an enterprise fund framework to track stormwater expenses and revenues. The committee emphasized that implementing any fees would require a separate, subsequent Town Meeting vote. Board members noted the accounting model could eventually allow Southborough to distribute stormwater management costs across all properties based on impervious surface, including tax-exempt parcels.

top_items.title: Governance study consultant presents municipal structure review
top_items.why: Consultant Bill Keegan presented initial findings on Southborough's governance model, town manager powers, and committee oversight to the Select Board.
top_items.body: Capital Strategic Strategies consultant Bill Keegan delivered an overview of Southborough's municipal government structure to the Select Board, comparing local practices with other Massachusetts communities. The presentation reviewed town manager statutory authority, committee coordination, and structural options as part of an ongoing town governance study.
